findings.title: Spreadsheet-style Status Panel
findings.where: Right side of HUD (Arena, Road screens)
findings.problem: The 'CONDITION' panel presents data as a dense list of text rows ('Front', 'Rear', 'FL', 'FR') with tiny progress bars. It resembles an Excel sheet more than a vehicle dashboard.
findings.why: At driving speeds, players cannot scan rows of small text quickly. This creates high cognitive load and obscures the viewing area, making it hard to assess vehicle health during combat.
findings.fix: Replace the text list with a compact visual widget. Use a central 'Hull Integrity' gauge surrounded by color-coded arcs (Green/Red) for armor sectors, or a simplified 4-quadrant status display.

findings.title: Leaked Debug Terminology
findings.problem: The text reads 'Screencap Rig' and 'Not road-legal'. The term 'Screencap' refers to a development tool function, not a game asset.
findings.why: This immediately breaks immersion and signals to the player that the UI is unfinished or that development debug logs have leaked into the build.
findings.fix: Rename the label to 'Current Chassis' or 'Vehicle Loadout'. Ensure all UI text uses consistent in-universe terminology.

findings.title: Disconnected Weapon Inventory
findings.problem: Weapons are listed numerically ('Weapon 1' through '10') in a plain text list, while the car visual is isolated on the right. Additionally, a yellow vertical bar appears on the left edge of every list item, creating visual noise.
findings.why: Players cannot intuitively map the text list to the physical mounting locations on the car. The stray yellow bars distract from the actual content.
findings.fix: Remove the generic yellow bars. Implement a direct link where selecting a weapon slot highlights the corresponding physical socket on the car visualization (e.g., hover 'Weapon 1' -> highlight 'Front Mount').

findings.title: Indistinct Waypoint Markers
findings.problem: The directional arrows indicating actions (blue, yellow, red) floating above buildings are low-opacity and blend significantly into the grey concrete floor.
findings.why: Objective clarity is crucial in a hub world. Faded colors reduce reaction time and make it difficult to distinguish between 'Fight', 'Build', and 'Care' stations at a glance.
findings.fix: Apply a bold white or black outline (stroke) to the arrows and increase their saturation/contrast to ensure they pop against the neutral environment textures.

findings.title: Passive Radar Design
findings.problem: The radar is a flat black circle with a faint green wedge. It lacks clear grid lines, cardinal direction markers, or high-contrast target indicators.
findings.why: In a combat game, threat detection must be instantaneous. A low-contrast 'monitor' aesthetic forces the player to strain to find enemies, especially if enemies are also dark or moving fast.
findings.fix: Draw distinct concentric rings for range and crosshairs for North/South. Use bright, pulsating distinct shapes (e.g., red squares or triangles) for enemy contacts rather than subtle dots.
